_doc: Home Assistant to an agentic PR. One entry per scene; sentences are cues. Numbers in words. Re-run narrate.py after any change.

en: Home Assistant ships a new release every month, with betas the week before.
For a custom integration, any of them can break something.
This heat pump integration used to check PyPI every six hours, from a cron job.
Late, wasteful, and blind to everything but that one index.
Now Angelia watches the Home Assistant releases on GitHub.
The calendar version scheme makes betas count as pre-releases.
And a one hour cooldown lets the wheel reach PyPI before anyone acts.
When a release lands, Angelia sends a repository dispatch to the integration's repository.
It carries the package, the version, the bump, and a stable event id.
A workflow validates the payload, then installs that exact Home Assistant version.
The import smoke test and the unit tests run against it, before anyone reads a changelog.
If this month's release has no review yet, Claude reads the release notes and the diff of the Home Assistant code the integration builds on.
It has no tools. It can only write a report.
When the maintainer adds a label, an agent prepares the fix, confined to the integration and its tests.
It opens a pull request, for a human to review.
One release, one event, and a human always in charge. The full recipe is in the Angelia docs.
